source.title: Unlearning's Blind Spots: Over-Unlearning and Prototypical Relearning Attack
source.authors: SeungBum Ha; Saerom Park; Sung Whan Yoon

record.file_problem: none; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests post-unlearning recovery in image-classification and face-recognition settings, extending relearning-attack findings to a different modality and class-level task.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates fine-tuning-based relearning attacks and its own prototype-based classifier-head attack (PRA). Rows below record the reported forgotten-class accuracy after attacks; they do not treat cited findings as results. OU@ε and retention-only results are not catalogued unless paired with an attack result. Table 2 reports before→after PRA values when Spotter is added.
record.test_reason: The study runs relearning attacks on unlearned vision classifiers (ResNet-18, ViT-S, DeiT-S on CIFAR, Tiny-ImageNet and CASIA-WebFace). It reports forgotten-class accuracy after a fine-tuning relearn attack (Fig. 2a) and after its own prototype head-patch attack (PRA). It also proposes a counter-method, Spotter. This is a new setting (class-level image unlearning, not LLM knowledge unlearning), so every verdict applies only to that setting. A key control: PRA on the retrained model, which never saw the class, already gives 58.70 (CIFAR-10) and 44.58 (CIFAR-100). Recovery counts as evidence of hidden residue only above that level.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that conventional class-level unlearning over-unlearns near the forget boundary (OU@ε), and that Spotter 'neutralizes' PRA while preserving utility. They acknowledge that Spotter has no formal guarantee and that PRA is a white-box audit.
record.recipe_differences: Class-level vision unlearning rather than LLM unlearning; PRA computes prototypes from labeled forget images and patches classifier-head parameters rather than fine-tuning or quantizing model weights. The attack blends prototype parameters with the existing head using α.
record.method_sensitivity: PRA recovery varies by unlearning method and dataset, and by interpolation factor α. Spotter resistance varies with λ2; the paper also reports recovery across prototype sample counts and model architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Unlearning causes collateral damage concentrated on retained samples near the forget class (OU@ε; Top-2/5/10% accuracy drops in Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class-level unlearning degrades retained data near the forget boundary even when global retained accuracy stays high.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306 (2026), as stated in the paper.
record.problems: The tests are class-level image and face-recognition tasks, not LLMs. Fine-tuning attack outcomes are described qualitatively and shown only in Figure 2(a), without numerical values in the text. The main results are averaged over three runs but no uncertainty intervals are reported. PRA is explicitly a white-box attack; limited-access attacks are left for future work.
record.rows_left_out: Left out separate Acc*r rows from Tables 1–2 and additional Spotter utility metrics because the catalog rows focus on forgotten-class recovery; left out Tables 11–12 sequential and severe-unlearning rows, which report more Spotter PRA outcomes in further settings. Table 7 includes only selected α conditions to show the outcome change; other methods and α values are not extracted. OU@ε and retained-accuracy-only results are not findings on the specified recovery versions.

untested.parts: LLM knowledge unlearning (WMDP-style), and general language ability.
Unrelated or loosely related relearning data, multi-epoch fine-tuning, LLMs, and fine-tuning attacks against Spotter.
Ablation of an activation direction. The internal edit tested is a classifier-head patch.
Prompting, jailbreaks, languages and in-context recovery, none of which are tested.
Spotter is tested only against the authors' own PRA. It is not tested against fine-tuning relearning, quantization, prompting, or adaptive and black-box attacks.

missing.what: λ1/λ2 ablation: Proto-Accf of about 91–99.9 at λ2=0, falling to ≤0.76 at λ2=1–2, with a few points' Accrt cost
Retrain, DELETE, SalUn and Boundary Shrink across the α sweep. The retrain values are needed as controls for r42–r46.

record.verdict_notes: The whole study is on vision classifiers, not LLMs; treat every verdict as a cross-modality analog. The retrain model's high PRA accuracy (58.70 / 44.58 / 78.90 on CASIA) shows that much of PRA's recovery reflects general feature quality, not hidden residue. Rows were therefore judged against that control. For F rows, state describes whether Spotter resists the attack. Spotter was evaluated only against the authors' own PRA, not against fine-tuning relearning.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests class-level vision unlearning and PRA, not LLM unlearning or general ability across language tasks.
Tests fine-tuning-based attacks on CIFAR-10, not unrelated or loosely related examples, other prompt formats, or language models.
Tests prototype-based classifier-head replacement and analyzes residual class features; it does not ablate an activation direction.
Prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context recovery.
Spotter is evaluated against PRA in vision models, not against quantization or prompting attacks, and not in LLMs.

source_check.notes: PRA is white-box, and Spotter has no formal guarantee and is tested only against the authors' own PRA. Read Proto-Accf against the large retrain controls (58.70, 44.58, 30.98, 78.90); Table 1 tunes alpha per method so that Acc*r >= Accr-1%. Table 7's alpha=1 values (UNSC 74.78, DELETE 90.92) differ from Table 1's, and the text does not say why.
